newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian leaders hope to woo German investors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian leaders hope to woo German investors.

text.p: Bulgaria's outgoing and incoming prime ministers visit Germany this week to try to attract investment to support their plans for economic reform.

Interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski leaves on Tuesday, to be joined on Wednesday by Ivan Kostov, leader of the Union of Democratic Forces, once the president has formally asked him to form a government.

The government press office said companies invited to their presentation by organisers Deutsche Bank AG included BASF AG, Bayer, Deutsche Telekom, Hoechst, Siemens, and the Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung (WAZ) press group which owns several Bulgarian newspapers.

"My task in Germany will be to assure foreign investors that Bulgaria is a good place to invest their capital. This is an easy task because we have achieved national consensus on the principles to lead the country out of crisis," Kostov told reporters on Monday.

Germany is Bulgaria's biggest foreign investor. Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel visited in March and promised German support for the Balkan country as it embarked on reforms already far advanced in other former East Bloc states.
Kostov said his presentation would emphasise measures agreed with the International Monetary Fund, including implementation of a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism known as a currency board.

"We will play an active role in the international sovereign debt markets through new debt instruments which the country will offer at an effective price that will decrease the investment risk for foreign investors," he said.
Foreign investors are already showing great interest in Bulgarian government securities which offer high yields and the security of the currency board, whose introduction is expected in July.

Kostov said he would also stress the fight against organised crime, and inform potential investors on the planned privatisation of 22 state-owned enterprises including Balkan Airlines, the Neftochim refinery, shipyards and steelworks. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188, 981 4145
